title: US Military Creates Four-Star Command to Advance AI Warfare
key_facts: Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth announced an Autonomous Warfare Command to be led by a four-star officer.
Its purpose is to speed adoption of AI, autonomous systems, drones and robotics.
The Pentagon wants to field larger numbers of lower-cost autonomous systems alongside expensive conventional weapons.
Defense One says a 30 Sep 2026 Hegseth memo slates the command to launch by next October.
The Defense Post photo caption places Hegseth's State of the Force address at Quantico on 30 Sep 2026.
quote_evidence: The move reflects the Pentagon's push to field larger numbers of lower-cost autonomous systems alongside expensive conventional weapons.

The planned Autonomous Warfare Command, slated to launch by next October, will promote "not a particular drone, but the ability to adapt in combat" against "realistic opposition," according to a Sept. 30 memo from Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth
why_it_matters_hint: A four-star command signals the Pentagon treating autonomous weapons as a main line of effort, but it is a plan with a launch date a year out.
notes: The Defense Post text is a short summary; launch timing taken from Defense One. Hegseth's title appears as Secretary of War in the caption.
